mainTopic: Washing a baby after מילה on שבת, treating wounds on שבת, and doubtful cases of מילה
overview: The משנה allows washing a baby on שבת before and after his מילה, with sprinkling by hand but not with a vessel. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה allows washing even on the third day, which the פסוק about שכם shows is a time of danger. The גמרא asks how washing can be allowed if a vessel is forbidden. רב יהודה and רבה בר אבוה read the משנה as 'washing means sprinkling by hand.' רבא reads it instead as two days: normal washing on the first day and only sprinkling on the third day. A ברייתא supports רבא, but he later regrets ruling against the elders, because the משנה's wording fits their reading. The הלכה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: the baby may be washed in every case, because he is in danger. The גמרא then discusses hot water, oil, and bandages on a wound on שבת. Finally, it begins the source for why a doubtful מילה does not override שבת, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Washing the baby before and after the circumcision
steps.stepSummary: The משנה permits washing a baby on שבת both before and after his מילה, and permits sprinkling water on him by hand but not with a vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: One may wash the baby on שבת, both before the circumcision and after it. One may sprinkle water on him by hand, but not with a vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the basic rule for caring for a baby on the day of his מילה when it falls on שבת. Washing is allowed, and sprinkling is allowed only by hand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Washing helps the baby's health around the מילה, so the משנה allows it on שבת. The limit, 'by hand but not with a vessel,' means doing it in an unusual way so it does not look like a normal weekday bath. On its own the wording looks contradictory: washing is allowed, yet a vessel is not. The גמרא will raise this in step 4.

keyTerms.meaning: A baby or small child (here, the baby being circumcised)

steps.confusionAlert: It sounds like two separate rules: full washing is allowed, and sprinkling is allowed only by hand. The גמרא will explain that the second clause actually describes HOW the washing is done.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One may wash the baby
phrases.notes: On שבת

phrases.english: both before the circumcision
and after the circumcision,
and one may sprinkle (water) on him by hand,
but not with a vessel.
phrases.notes: An unusual way of doing it, to set it apart from a normal weekday bath

steps.triggerLanguage: מַרְחִיצִין אֶת הַקָּטָן בֵּין לִפְנֵי הַמִּילָה וּבֵין לְאַחַר הַמִּילָה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבת one may wash a baby before and after מילה, and may sprinkle water on him by hand but not with a vessel.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: washing on the third day
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה rules that one may wash the baby on the third day after מילה even if it falls on שבת. He learns from the men of שכם, who were in pain on the third day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says: one may wash the baby on the third day after the circumcision even if that day falls on שבת. As the verse says: 'And it came to pass on the third day, when they were in pain.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה extends the permission to wash the baby to the third day after the מילה, even on שבת. He brings a פסוק to show that the third day is especially painful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the men of שכם (בראשית ל״ד) shows that the third day after מילה is the hardest and most dangerous. Danger to life (פיקוח נפש) overrides שבת, so washing the baby is allowed on that day too. This adds a new day to the first rule, which covered only the day of the מילה itself.

keyTerms.meaning: That happens to fall on שבת

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a source showing that the third day after מילה counts as a time of danger, which allows care for the baby on שבת.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:
One may wash the baby on the third day
phrases.notes: The third day after the circumcision

phrases.english: that happens to fall on Shabbat,
as it is stated: 'And it came to pass on the third day
phrases.notes: Said about the men of שכם after their circumcision (בראשית 34:25)

phrases.english: when they were in pain.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the washing permission from the day of the מילה to the third day after it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may wash the baby on the third day after מילה even on שבת, because that day is dangerous.

steps.title: Doubtful cases and a hermaphrodite baby
steps.stepSummary: For a ספק case or an אנדרוגינוס, one does not break שבת to do the מילה. רבי יהודה permits it for an אנדרוגינוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a doubtful case, and for a baby with both male and female organs, one does not break שבת to circumcise him. רבי יהודה permits it for the baby with both organs.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new topic: cases where it is unclear whether the מילה is required on שבת. The תנא קמא says not to break שבת, and רבי יהודה disagrees about the אנדרוגינוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מילה overrides שבת only when it is clearly a required מילה on its proper eighth day. In a ספק, for example a baby born at בין השמשות so it is unclear which day is the eighth, the requirement is uncertain, so שבת is not broken. רבי יהודה holds that an אנדרוגינוס is obligated in מילה, so for him it overrides שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubtful case (e.g., unclear whether today is truly the eighth day)
A person with both male and female organs

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה is not saying these babies get no מילה at all. It only says that in these cases the מילה does not override שבת; it can be done on a weekday.

phrases.english: A doubtful case and a hermaphrodite —
one does not desecrate Shabbat for him.
phrases.notes: To circumcise him

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda permits it for a hermaphrodite.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָפֵק וְאַנְדְּרוֹגִינוֹס אֵין מְחַלְּלִין עָלָיו אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic in the משנה: uncertain obligations of מילה on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One does not break שבת to circumcise a ספק or an אנדרוגינוס; רבי יהודה permits it for an אנדרוגינוס.

steps.title: Washing is allowed, so why is sprinkling with a vessel forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: the first clause allows full washing, so how can the next clause forbid even sprinkling with a vessel?
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: But you said in the first clause, 'One may wash!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out an apparent contradiction inside the first part of the משנה. If washing is allowed, sprinkling with a vessel, which is less, should surely be allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Washing the whole body is more than sprinkling. So if the רישא allows washing, forbidding a vessel for mere sprinkling makes no sense. The challenge forces us to explain how the two clauses fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't you say? (opens a contradiction)

phrases.english: GEMARA: But didn't you say in the first clause: 'One may wash'!
phrases.notes: So why would sprinkling with a vessel be forbidden?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the first rule of the משנה (step 1) to challenge its internal consistency.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's clause 'sprinkle by hand but not with a vessel'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If full washing is permitted, then sprinkling with a vessel, a lesser act, should certainly be permitted. The two clauses seem to contradict.

steps.title: The משנה uses a 'how' structure
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה and רבה בר אבוה explain that the משנה is written in a 'כיצד' style: the second clause explains how the washing in the first clause is done, by sprinkling by hand only.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה and רבה בר אבוה both said: the משנה is taught with 'How?' It means: One may wash the baby before and after the circumcision. How? One sprinkles water on him by hand, but not with a vessel.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer the challenge by rereading the משנה. The second clause is not a separate rule; it explains the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With an unwritten 'כיצד' (how?) between the clauses, 'washing' does not mean a full bath. It means sprinkling water by hand. So there is no contradiction: washing is allowed only in this limited way, and a vessel is not allowed. The גמרא repeats the words of the משנה here to show the new reading.

keyTerms.meaning: How? (the second clause explains the first)

steps.whatToRemember: The 'washing' allowed in the משנה is not a full bath. It means sprinkling water by hand. The second clause explains the first through a 'כיצד' (how?) reading.
steps.whyThisMatters: The 'כיצד' reading is a common tool in the גמרא: what looks like two separate rules may really be a general rule followed by its explanation.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda and Rabba bar Avuh
who both said: Teach it with 'How?':
phrases.notes: The second clause explains the first

phrases.english: One may wash the baby

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין לִפְנֵי מִילָה בֵּין לְאַחַר מִילָה.
phrases.english: both before circumcision and after circumcision.
How?

phrases.aramaic: מְזַלְּפִין עָלָיו בַּיָּד אֲבָל לֹא בִּכְלִי.
phrases.english: One sprinkles on him by hand, but not with a vessel.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יְהוּדָה וְרַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ דְאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ כֵּיצַד תָּנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 4 by rereading the structure of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the text: the second clause explains the first (כיצד structure)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two independent rules: full washing is permitted, and separately sprinkling is limited to the hand.
steps.terutzMaskana: One rule: 'washing' means sprinkling by hand only, not with a vessel.

steps.title: רבא objects that the משנה says 'washing', not sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges the 'כיצד' answer. The משנה clearly says 'מרחיצין', which means real washing, so it cannot simply mean sprinkling by hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: But the משנה says 'one may wash'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the answer from step 5. He says the word in the משנה is 'washing', and washing is not the same as sprinkling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה and רבה בר אבוה said the משנה's 'washing' really means 'sprinkling by hand'. רבא says that reading twists the plain word 'מרחיצין'. A full washing and a little sprinkling are two different actions, so the earlier answer does not hold up.

keyTerms.meaning: but it teaches! (a challenge from the wording of the text)

phrases.english: Rava said:
But it teaches 'one may wash'!
phrases.notes: Washing is not sprinkling, so the 'כיצד' reading does not fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the 'כיצד' answer given in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'מרחיצין' in the משנה means sprinkling by hand.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plain meaning of 'מרחיצין' is full washing, which is a different act from sprinkling.

steps.title: רבא rereads the משנה as two different days
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the משנה describes two different days. On the first day after מילה, the baby is washed normally. On a third day that falls on שבת, the תנא קמא allows only sprinkling by hand. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה allows full washing even then.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said, this is what the משנה teaches: One may wash the baby, both before the circumcision and after the circumcision. On the first day, he is washed in the normal way. On the third day, if it falls on שבת, one sprinkles water on him by hand, but not with a vessel. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says: One may wash the baby on the third day if it falls on שבת, as it says: 'And it was on the third day, when they were in pain.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his own solution to the contradiction from step 4. The full washing and the sprinkling rule apply to different days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there is no contradiction: full washing is allowed on the first day, and sprinkling-only applies to a third day that falls on שבת. The מחלוקת between the תנא קמא and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה is only about that third day, which רבי אלעזר בן עזריה treats as a day of danger based on the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: this is what it teaches (a rereading of the text)
on the first day after the מילה
that happens to fall on שבת

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree that full washing is allowed on the first day. They argue only about the third day: the תנא קמא says sprinkle by hand only, and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says you may wash.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a clean מחלוקת about the third day, which the ברייתא in the next step confirms.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said,
this is what it teaches:
One may wash the baby
both before the circumcision
and after the circumcision.
On the first day, in the normal way.
And on the third day
that falls on Shabbat,
one sprinkles water on him by hand,
but not with a vessel.
Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:
One may wash the baby
on the third day
that falls on Shabbat,
as it says: 'And it was on the third day
when they were in pain.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the 'כיצד' answer, רבא offers a new way to resolve the contradiction from step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: the clauses refer to different days (day one versus day three).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The washing and the sprinkling seemed to describe the same situation, so they contradicted each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Washing applies to the first day, and sprinkling applies to the third day on שבת according to the תנא קמא.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports רבא's reading
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is quoted that matches רבא's reading exactly: normal washing on the first day, and sprinkling by hand on a third day that falls on שבת. It also adds that the verse about שכם is only a hint, not a full proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught in line with רבא: One may wash the baby both before and after the circumcision. On the first day, he is washed in the normal way. On the third day that falls on שבת, one sprinkles water on him by hand. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says: One may wash the baby on the third day that falls on שבת. And even though there is no proof for the matter, there is a hint to it, as it says: 'And it was on the third day, when they were in pain.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the same thing as רבא. This supports his reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא spells out the two-day structure in plain words. That confirms רבא's split between the first day and the third day. It also adds a new phrase: the שכם verse is only a 'זכר' (hint) and not a 'ראיה' (proof). The גמרא will explain that phrase in steps 10 and 11.

keyTerms.meaning: a ברייתא was taught in line with his view (support)
there is no proof for the matter

phrases.english: A Baraita was taught in line with Rava:
One may wash the baby
both before circumcision
and after circumcision.
On the first day, in the normal way.
And on the third day that falls on Shabbat,
one sprinkles water on him by hand.
Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:
One may wash the baby
on the third day that falls on Shabbat.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רְאָיָה לַדָּבָר
phrases.english: And even though there is no proof for the matter,
there is a hint to the matter,
as it says: 'And it was on the third day
when they were in pain.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support רבא's reading from step 7.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's reading of the משנה: normal washing on the first day and sprinkling on the third day.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the same two-day structure.

steps.title: The ברייתא's sprinkling rule follows the תנא קמא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that sprinkling may be done only by hand, not with a cup, a bowl, or any vessel. The גמרא notes that this line returns to the view of the תנא קמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when they sprinkle, they do not sprinkle with a cup, or with a bowl, or with any vessel, but only by hand. We have come back to the תנא קמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains how the sprinkling is done. The גמרא then points out whose opinion this detail belongs to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה allows full washing, so a rule about how to sprinkle cannot be his. This line must belong to the תנא קמא, even though it comes after רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's words in the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: we have come back to the first Tanna

steps.confusionAlert: This line comes right after רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, but it is not his view. It belongs to the תנא קמא.

phrases.english: And when they sprinkle,
they do not sprinkle with a cup,
or with a bowl, or with any vessel,
but only by hand.
We have come back to the first Tanna.
phrases.notes: A comment by the גמרא, not part of the ברייתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא and identifies whose view its last line follows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sprinkling on the third day is done only by hand, never with a vessel. This follows the תנא קמא.

steps.title: Why is the verse only a hint and not a proof?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא means when it says there is no proof, only a hint.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'even though there is no proof for the matter, there is a hint to the matter' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question to explain the ברייתא's phrase. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says clearly that the men of שכם were in pain on the third day after מילה. That sounds like a strong proof. So why does the ברייתא downgrade it to just a 'hint'?

phrases.aramaic: מַאי ״אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רְאָיָה לַדָּבָר
phrases.english: What does 'even though there is no proof for the matter,
there is a hint to the matter' mean?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי ״אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רְאָיָה לַדָּבָר זֵכֶר לַדָּבָר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a phrase in the ברייתא quoted in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the שכם verse counts only as a hint and not as a full proof.

steps.title: Adults heal slowly, but babies heal quickly
steps.stepSummary: The men of שכם were adults, and adult flesh heals slowly. A baby's flesh heals quickly, so a baby may not be in danger on the third day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because an adult's flesh does not heal quickly, but a baby's flesh heals quickly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The proof from שכם is weak because the men there were adults, not babies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse shows that adults are in pain on the third day. But a baby heals much faster, so we cannot be sure a baby is still in danger then. That is why the verse is only a 'זכר' (hint) for רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's ruling.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא: full washing on the first day. On a third day that falls on שבת, the תנא קמא allows only sprinkling by hand, while רבי אלעזר בן עזריה allows washing. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's verse is only a hint, because adults (like the men of שכם) heal slowly and babies heal quickly.

phrases.english: Because an adult,
his flesh does not heal quickly,
but a baby, his flesh heals quickly.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּגָדוֹל לָא סָלֵיק בִּישְׂרֵיהּ הַיָּיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse is about adults, who heal slowly. Babies heal quickly, so the verse cannot fully prove that a baby is in danger on the third day.

steps.title: רבא rules in practice, falls ill, and regrets it
steps.stepSummary: Someone asked רבא a practical question. רבא ruled according to his own explanation. Then רבא became ill and regretted going against the elders' explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain person came before רבא, and רבא ruled for him according to his own teaching. Then רבא became sick and said: 'Why did I get involved with the explanation of the elders?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story: רבא put his reading of the משנה into practice, then got sick and took it as a sign that he should not have argued with the earlier sages. This story sets up the next exchange.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's ruling followed his reading from Step 7: full washing on the first day, and only sprinkling on a third day that falls on שבת. 'The elders' (רב יהודה and רבה בר אבוה) had explained the משנה more strictly. In their reading, the תנא קמא allows only sprinkling, even on the first day. רבא saw his illness as a punishment for taking their view lightly.

keyTerms.meaning: He ruled for him (gave a practical הוראה)
According to his own teaching or reading
The explanation of the elders (the earlier sages' reading)

steps.whyThisMatters: The story shows how seriously the חכמים treated a practical ruling that disagreed with earlier authorities.

phrases.english: A certain person who came before Rava,
he ruled for him according to his own teaching.
phrases.notes: That is, washing is permitted on the first day.

phrases.english: Rava became ill, and he said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲנָא בַּהֲדֵי תַּרְגּוּמָא דְסָבֵי לְמָה לִי.
phrases.english: Why did I get involved with the explanation of the elders?
phrases.notes: The elders are רב יהודה and רבה בר אבוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבא's theoretical reading (Steps 7–11) to a story about his practical ruling and his regret.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא ruled according to his own reading, then regretted disagreeing with the elders' stricter reading.

steps.title: The רבנן point out that a ברייתא supports רבא
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן challenge רבא's regret: a ברייתא was taught exactly like his view, so why worry?
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן said to רבא: 'But wasn't a ברייתא taught in agreement with you, Master?'
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן question why רבא regrets his ruling, since a ברייתא backs him up. This sets up רבא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This refers to the ברייתא from Step 8, which matches רבא's reading exactly. If an early source supports him, his ruling seems well grounded, so his regret looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: In agreement with the Master (meaning you)

phrases.english: The Rabbis said to Rava:
But wasn't a baraita taught in accordance with the Master?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions רבא's regret from Step 12 by pointing to the ברייתא from Step 8.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An explicit ברייתא supports רבא, so he has no reason to worry that he ruled wrongly.

steps.title: רבא answers that the משנה's wording fits the elders
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that even though the ברייתא supports him, the precise wording of the משנה supports the elders.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: 'Our משנה, read carefully, fits their view.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains why the ברייתא does not calm him: the משנה itself, read closely, supports the elders. The next step shows the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא sets two sources against each other. A careful reading of the משנה carries great weight, so the ברייתא is not enough to override it. That is why he still worries.

keyTerms.meaning: Is precise (a close reading of the wording shows it)

phrases.english: He said to them:
Our mishna is precise in accordance with them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Weighing sources: the close reading of the משנה outweighs the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא proves רבא right, so his regret is unfounded.
steps.terutzMaskana: The wording of the משנה supports the elders, so רבא's concern is justified.

steps.title: Proof from the word 'wash' in רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's statement
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says only 'one may wash,' not 'one may even wash.' That fits a תנא קמא who allows only sprinkling, even on the first day.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we see this? From the fact that רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says: 'One may wash the baby on the third day that falls on שבת.' If the תנא קמא said only 'one may sprinkle,' it makes sense that רבי אלעזר בן עזריה answered him 'one may wash.' But if the תנא קמא said one may wash on the first day and sprinkle on the third, then רבי אלעזר בן עזריה should have said 'one may EVEN wash.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows exactly how the משנה's wording supports the elders: the word רבי אלעזר בן עזריה chose makes the most sense if the תנא קמא never allowed washing at all on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תנא קמא allowed only sprinkling, then רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's plain 'one may wash' is a direct disagreement. If the תנא קמא already allowed washing on the first day, then רבי אלעזר בן עזריה would only be adding the third day. In that case the natural wording is 'even wash,' and the missing 'אף' suggests the elders' reading is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, if you say (this reading works well)
Even (adds to what was already allowed)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי אלעזר בן עזריה is changing his view here. The whole proof hangs on one missing word, 'אף' (even). That missing word tells us what the תנא קמא must have said.

phrases.english: From where?

phrases.aramaic: מִדְּקָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: From that it says: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:
One may wash the baby
on the third day that falls on Shabbat.
Granted, if you say
that the first tanna says only 'one may sprinkle,'
phrases.notes: This is the elders' reading: sprinkling only, even on the first day.

phrases.english: that explains why he says to him,
Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya: 'One may wash.'
But if you say that the first tanna
says one may wash on the first day,
phrases.notes: This is רבא's reading.

phrases.english: and one may sprinkle on the third day,

phrases.aramaic: הַאי רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אוֹמֵר מַרְחִיצִין
phrases.english: then this statement, 'Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says one may wash' —
he should have said 'one may EVEN wash'!

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי מִדְּקָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the proof behind רבא's claim in Step 14.
steps.raayaObject: The elders' reading: the תנא קמא allows only sprinkling on שבת, even on the first day.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The wording of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה in the משנה: 'מרחיצין' without 'אף'.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports in the name of רבי אלעזר that the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל, he said in the name of רבי אלעזר: 'The הלכה is like רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the practical ruling: the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה allows full washing even on the third day when it falls on שבת. So in practice, the baby may be washed normally, whichever reading of the תנא קמא is correct. This ruling makes the argument between רבא and the elders less important in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

steps.whatToRemember: The הלכה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: a baby may be washed normally after מילה, even on the third day when it falls on שבת.
steps.confusionAlert: There are two different people here. רבי אלעזר (no 'בן עזריה') is an אמורא who gives the ruling. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה is the תנא from the משנה whose view becomes the הלכה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical law for caring for a newborn after מילה on שבת.

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came
he said that Rabbi Elazar said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the discussion with the practical ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: full washing of the baby is permitted even on the third day after מילה when it falls on שבת.

steps.title: Whole body or only the place of the circumcision?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים in ארץ ישראל ask what kind of washing is being discussed: washing the baby's whole body, or only washing the place of the מילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked in the West (ארץ ישראל): Is this talking about washing his whole body, or washing the place of the מילה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about the ruling it just accepted. Now that we hold like רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, we need to know what kind of washing he allows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה permits washing the baby on the third day when it falls on שבת. The question is how much he permits: the whole body, or only the wound area. This question sets up the debate that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The West.' This means ארץ ישראל, which is west of בבל.
'They discussed it.' The חכמים were unsure about it.
Washing only the place of the circumcision

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether washing is allowed. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה already allows it. The question is only how much of the baby may be washed.

phrases.english: They discussed it in the West (Eretz Yisrael):
Is it washing his whole body
or washing the place of the circumcision?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, the גמרא asks what his ruling covers.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי אלעזר בן עזריה permits washing the whole body or only the מילה area.

steps.title: רבי יעקב: it must mean the whole body
steps.stepSummary: רבי יעקב argues that the washing must be of the whole body. Washing just the wound is no worse than putting hot water on a wound, which רב already permits on שבת, so it would not need a special ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: One of the חכמים, named רבי יעקב, said to them: It makes sense that it means washing his whole body. If you thought it meant washing only the מילה, is that any worse than hot water on a wound? רב said: We do not prevent hot water and oil from being put on a wound on שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יעקב answers the question: the ruling must be about the whole body. He proves it from a ruling of רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב already allows hot water and oil on any wound on שבת. A מילה wound is a wound, so washing it would obviously be allowed. Therefore רבי אלעזר בן עזריה must be adding something new: permission to wash the whole body.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It makes sense.' A logical argument is coming.
'Is it any worse?' This compares two cases to show one is at least as allowed as the other.
'We do not prevent.' It is permitted.

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key question that follows: is hot water on a wound really the same as our case?

phrases.english: One of the Sages said to them,
and Rabbi Ya'akov was his name:
It makes sense that it means washing his whole body,
for if you think it means washing the circumcision,

phrases.aramaic: מִי גָּרַע מֵחַמִּין עַל גַּבֵּי מַכָּה,
phrases.english: is it any worse than hot water on a wound?
For Rav said:
We do not prevent hot water and oil
from being put on a wound on Shabbat!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ הַהוּא מֵרַבָּנַן, וְרַבִּי יַעֲקֹב שְׁמֵיהּ: מִסְתַּבְּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ruling refers to washing the whole body, because washing just the wound is already permitted under רב's ruling.

steps.title: רב יוסף: water heated on שבת is different
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף rejects רבי יעקב's proof. רב's case uses water heated before שבת. Our case uses water heated on שבת, which is a much more serious matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objected: Don't you see a difference between hot water heated on שבת and hot water heated before שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks רבי יעקב's comparison. He says the two cases are not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Putting water heated before שבת on a wound only involves a rabbinic concern about healing. Heating water on שבת itself is a Torah-level מלאכה. So רב's ruling cannot prove that washing the מילה with water heated on שבת is allowed. That means רבי אלעזר בן עזריה could be talking about the מילה alone after all.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He strongly objected to it.' This introduces a sharp challenge.
Water heated on שבת itself, which involves a Torah prohibition

steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not disagreeing with רב's ruling. He agrees hot water on a wound is allowed. He only says that ruling is about water heated before שבת, so it does not match our case.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef objected strongly:
And is there no difference for you
between hot water heated on Shabbat
and hot water heated on Shabbat eve?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof רבי יעקב brought in step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יעקב's comparison to רב's ruling about hot water on a wound.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב's case uses water heated before שבת, which is only a rabbinic issue. Our case uses water heated on שבת, which is a Torah prohibition. The proof does not carry over.

steps.title: רב דימי: maybe the dispute is about water heated before שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי challenges רב יוסף: how do we know the case is about water heated on שבת? Maybe it is about water heated before שבת, in which case רבי יעקב's proof works.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי objected: How do you know they are arguing here about water heated on שבת? Maybe they are arguing about water heated before שבת?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי pushes back on רב יוסף. He questions the assumption that our case uses water heated on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's objection only works if the case involves water heated on שבת. If the case is about water heated before שבת, it matches רב's case, and רבי יעקב's proof stands. So רב דימי asks for evidence that the case involves heating on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And from where do we know?' This asks for proof of an assumption.

phrases.english: Rav Dimi objected strongly:
And from where do you know that here
they disagree about hot water heated on Shabbat?

phrases.aramaic: דִילְמָא בְּחַמִּין שֶׁהוּחַמּוּ בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת פְּלִיגִי?!
phrases.english: Perhaps they disagree about hot water heated on Shabbat eve?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption behind רב יוסף's objection in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's assumption that the case involves water heated on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nothing in the text says the water was heated on שבת. If it was heated before שבת, רב יוסף's distinction disappears and רבי יעקב's proof returns.

steps.title: The baby is in danger, so it must be heating on שבת
steps.stepSummary: אביי reports that רב יוסף answered first, with the answer אביי had wanted to give: the case involves danger to the baby. That shows the discussion is about heating water on שבת itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: I wanted to answer him, but רב יוסף answered first: Because it is a danger for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers רב דימי's challenge, and אביי says he had planned the same answer. The answer is that the baby is in danger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Danger to life is a reason strong enough to permit even a Torah-level מלאכה, such as heating water on שבת. The reason given for washing the baby is danger, so the discussion must be about heating on שבת itself. That means רב יוסף's distinction stands, and רבי יעקב's proof from רב is rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he got ahead.' He answered first.
Danger to life, which can override שבת prohibitions

steps.whatToRemember: Washing a baby after מילה on the third day is treated as a matter of danger. That is why the discussion is about heating water on שבת itself. רבי יעקב's proof from hot water on a wound, which used water heated before שבת, does not decide whether the whole body or only the מילה may be washed.
steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not adding a new opinion. He is telling us that רב יוסף gave the answer he himself had in mind.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
I wanted to answer him,
but Rav Yosef answered him first:
Because it is a danger for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: אֲנָא בְּעַאי דֶּאֱישַׁנֵּי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב דימי's challenge from step 20 and supports רב יוסף's objection from step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proves the case definition from the reason given for the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Maybe the dispute concerns water heated before שבת, which would let רבי יעקב's proof stand.
steps.terutzMaskana: The reason is danger, which only needs to be invoked to permit heating on שבת. So the case is about water heated on שבת, and the proof from רב does not apply.

steps.title: The ruling: washing is allowed in every case because of danger
steps.stepSummary: רבין reports in the name of רבי אבהו that the הלכה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה in all cases. This covers water heated on שבת or before שבת, and washing the whole body or only the מילה, because it is dangerous for the baby.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: When רבין came, he said in the name of רבי אבהו in the name of רבי אלעזר (and some say רבי אבהו in the name of רבי יוחנן): The הלכה follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. This applies whether the water was heated on שבת or before שבת, and whether it is washing the whole body or only the place of the מילה, because it is a danger for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an outside report that settles the whole discussion from the earlier steps. Washing the baby is permitted in every version of the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the חכמים argued about whether the washing meant the whole body or just the wound, and whether the water was heated on שבת or before. This report says the question does not matter for the הלכה: all four cases are permitted. The reason is the same one אביי and רב יוסף gave in Step 21: the baby is in danger.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated (an outside report that supports what was just said)
When רבין came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

steps.whatToRemember: Final הלכה: we wash a baby after מילה on שבת in all cases, with water heated on שבת or before, the whole body or just the מילה, because not doing so is dangerous.
steps.whyThisMatters: The reason of סכנה is what lets even water heated on שבת be used. This matches רב יוסף's answer in Step 21, which אביי had also wanted to give.

phrases.english: It was also stated:
When Ravin came (from Eretz Yisrael)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר,
phrases.english: he said that Rabbi Abbahu said in the name of Rabbi Elazar,
and some say it this way:
phrases.notes: Here's a second version of how this was passed down.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
The halacha follows Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya
both with hot water heated on Shabbat,
and with hot water heated before Shabbat;
both washing his whole body,
and washing only the place of the milah,
because it is a danger for him (the baby).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the danger reasoning of Step 21 and settles the questions of Step 17 by permitting every case.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Washing a baby after מילה on שבת is permitted in all cases (water heated on שבת or before, whole body or just the מילה) because of סכנה.

steps.title: רב and שמואל disagree about hot water and oil on a wound
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to רב's statement quoted earlier. רב says we do not stop someone from putting hot water and oil on a wound on שבת. שמואל says it must be put next to the wound so it flows down onto it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The matter itself: רב said, we do not prevent hot water and oil from being put on a wound on שבת. And שמואל said: one puts it outside the wound, and it flows down onto the wound.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. It studies רב's statement about wounds, which was mentioned in passing in Step 18, and adds שמואל's opposing view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב allows putting hot water and oil directly on the wound. שמואל is stricter: putting it directly on looks like medical treatment, so you must put it above the wound and let it drip down. This disagreement sets up the challenges that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself: going back to fully study a statement that was quoted earlier

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל does not forbid the water and oil from reaching the wound. He only changes how you put it there, so it does not look like medical treatment.

phrases.english: The matter itself:
Rav said:
We do not prevent hot water and oil
from being placed on a wound on Shabbat.
And Shmuel said:
One places it outside the wound,
and it flows and drips down onto the wound.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the washing topic and fully studies רב's wound ruling that רבי יעקב cited in Step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: hot water and oil may be placed directly on a wound on שבת. שמואל: only next to the wound, letting it flow onto it.

steps.title: A ברייתא forbids putting oil and hot water on a cloth for a wound
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says you may not put oil and hot water on a soft cloth to place it on a wound on שבת. This seems to contradict רב's permission.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: We do not put oil and hot water on a soft cloth in order to place it on a wound on שבת!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב from a ברייתא that seems to forbid treating a wound with hot water and oil on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If treating a wound with oil and hot water were allowed, as רב says, why would the ברייתא forbid it? The challenge assumes the ברייתא forbids it because it looks like medical treatment, which fits שמואל's view better.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
We do not put oil and hot water
on a soft cloth
in order to place it on a wound on Shabbat!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב's ruling from Step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that hot water and oil may be put on a wound on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids applying oil and hot water to a wound by cloth. This suggests that treating a wound this way is forbidden, against רב.

steps.title: The cloth is forbidden only because of squeezing
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's ban is about the cloth, because you might squeeze the liquid out of it. It is not a ban on treating the wound.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is because of squeezing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב by explaining that the ברייתא has a different reason for its ban.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Soaking a cloth in liquid creates a risk of squeezing it, which is a forbidden מלאכה on שבת. So the problem is the cloth, not the healing. Without a cloth, רב's permission still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Squeezing liquid out of cloth, forbidden on שבת

phrases.english: There, it is because of squeezing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different reason: the ban comes from a separate concern (סחיטה), not from medical treatment.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא forbids treating a wound with oil and hot water, against רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only forbids using a soaked cloth because of the risk of squeezing. Applying directly is still allowed according to רב.

steps.title: A second ברייתא: not even onto a cloth already on the wound
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא forbids putting hot water and oil on a cloth that is already lying on a wound on שבת. This again seems to go against רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: We do not put hot water and oil on a soft cloth that is on a wound on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge to רב from a similar ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the cloth is already on the wound, so you are only pouring liquid onto it, not wringing a cloth to place it. Since the ban still applies even in this case, it seems the problem must be treating the wound itself, against רב.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
We do not put hot water and oil
on a soft cloth
that is on a wound, on Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אֵין נוֹתְנִין חַמִּין וָשֶׁמֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, stronger challenge to רב after the first one was answered in Step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that hot water and oil may be put on a wound on שבת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even pouring onto a cloth already resting on the wound is forbidden. So it seems the ban is about treating the wound, not about squeezing.

steps.title: Here too, the reason is squeezing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this ברייתא also forbids it only because of squeezing the cloth.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, it is because of squeezing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב again with the same answer: the problem is the cloth and the risk of squeezing it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even when a cloth is already on the wound, pouring liquid onto it soaks it and could lead to squeezing. So this ברייתא also does not forbid the healing itself, and רב's ruling survives.
steps.whatToRemember: Both ברייתות that forbid oil and hot water on a wound are about using a cloth, which risks סחיטה. They do not disprove רב's permission to put hot water and oil directly on a wound on שבת.

phrases.english: There too, it is because of squeezing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 26 with the same reasoning used in Step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different reason: the ban is because of סחיטה, not because of healing.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since even pouring onto a cloth already on the wound is forbidden, treating a wound must be forbidden, against רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Soaking any cloth risks squeezing. That is the only reason for the ban, so רב stands.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports שמואל's way of applying oil and hot water
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is brought that matches שמואל: oil and hot water may not go directly on the wound on שבת, but they may be put next to it so they flow down onto it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with שמואל: One may not put hot water and oil directly on a wound on שבת. But one may put them outside the wound, and they flow and run down onto the wound.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what שמואל said: put the liquid next to the wound, not on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 23, שמואל said the liquid must be put beside the wound so it flows onto it. This ברייתא gives the same rule word for word, so שמואל's opinion now has support from an earlier source. Putting it directly on the wound looks like normal medical treatment. Letting it flow down from the side is an indirect way of doing it.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with him

phrases.english: A baraita was taught in accordance with Shmuel:
phrases.notes: This phrase means an earlier source backs up what the אמורא said.

phrases.english: One may not place hot water and oil
directly on a wound on Shabbat,
but one may place it outside the wound,
and it flows and runs down onto the wound.
phrases.notes: This is the same method שמואל described in step 23.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenges to רב are answered, the גמרא brings a source that supports שמואל's method.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's rule that the liquid goes next to the wound so it flows onto it
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with exactly the same wording
steps.whatToRemember: On שבת, hot water and oil go next to the wound and flow onto it. They are not put directly on it.

steps.title: Which dry materials may be put on a wound
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא allows putting dry cotton padding and a dry sponge on a wound on שבת. It forbids a dry reed and dry rags.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: One may put dry cotton padding and a dry sponge on a wound. But one may not put a dry reed or dry rags on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that lists what dry things may and may not be put on a wound on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The padding and sponge are allowed because they only protect the wound. The reed and the rags are forbidden because they actually help heal it, which counts as medical treatment. Notice that מוך is itself a kind of rag. This sets up the contradiction in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Soft padding made from worn-out cloth, a kind of rag

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: נוֹתְנִין עַל גַּבֵּי הַמַּכָּה
phrases.english: The Sages taught: One may place on a wound
dry padding and a dry sponge,
but not a dry reed
and not dry rags.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: נוֹתְנִין עַל גַּבֵּי הַמַּכָּה מוֹךְ יָבֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a new ברייתא about wound care. It moves from liquids to dry bandages.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dry padding and a dry sponge are allowed on a wound on שבת. A dry reed and dry rags are not.

steps.title: Rags allowed and rags forbidden in the same ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out a contradiction: the ברייתא allows מוך, which is rags, and then forbids rags.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a difficulty: the rule about rags contradicts the rule about rags!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא because it seems to contradict itself about rags.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מוך is made of rags, and the ברייתא allows it. Then the same ברייתא forbids כתיתין, which are also rags. It does not make sense to allow and forbid the same material.

phrases.english: There is a difficulty: rags contradict rags!
phrases.notes: The first 'rags' means the מוך that was allowed. The second means the כתיתין that were forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This challenges the internal consistency of the ברייתא in step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two halves of the ברייתא in step 29
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same material, rags, is allowed in the first half (as מוך) and forbidden in the second half (as כתיתין).
steps.confusionAlert: The word כתיתין only shows up once in the ברייתא. The 'first rags' is the מוך, which is a type of rag.

steps.title: New rags versus old rags
steps.stepSummary: The contradiction is resolved: the forbidden rags are new ones, which heal, and the allowed rags are old ones, which do not heal.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This ruling, which forbids, is about new rags. That ruling, which allows, is about old rags.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by saying the two rulings are about two different kinds of rags.
steps.deeperAnalysis: New rags help heal a wound, so putting them on is medical treatment and is forbidden on שבת. Old, worn rags do not heal. They only cover and protect the wound, so they are allowed. There is no contradiction, because the two cases are different.

phrases.english: It is not difficult: this one is about new rags,
phrases.notes: New rags are forbidden because they heal.

phrases.english: and that one is about old rags.
phrases.notes: Old rags are allowed because they only protect.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא בְּחַדְתֵי, הָא בְּעַתִּיקֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers the contradiction raised in step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (הא בהא): the two rulings refer to different types of rags
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Rags are a single category, so the ברייתא seems to both allow and forbid them.
steps.terutzMaskana: New rags heal and are forbidden. Old rags do not heal and are allowed.

steps.title: אביי learns that rags heal
steps.stepSummary: אביי concludes from this answer that rags have healing power.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Learn from this that these rags heal.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי takes a practical lesson from the answer: new rags really do heal wounds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only reason the גמרא could forbid new rags is that they count as healing. So the answer itself tells us a fact about medicine: rags heal. אביי points this out as useful information.

phrases.english: Abaye said: Learn from this
that these rags heal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This draws a practical lesson from the answer in step 31.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: New rags have real healing power, which is why they are forbidden on a wound on שבת.
steps.whatToRemember: On שבת, things that only protect a wound (dry padding, a sponge, old rags) are allowed. Things that heal it (a reed, new rags) are forbidden.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: a doubtful baby and a hermaphrodite
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words about a ספק and an אנדרוגינוס, to begin discussing that part of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: "A doubtful case and a hermaphrodite," and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new topic. It quotes the next line of the משנה so it can explain it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה taught that we do not break שבת to do מילה for a baby whose status is in doubt, or for an אנדרוגינוס. The גמרא now looks for the source of this rule. The next step brings it.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubtful case, here a baby whose status for מילה on the eighth day is uncertain
A person with both male and female features
Etc., and so on: the quote continues

phrases.english: A doubtful case and a hermaphrodite, etc.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה, the heading for the next discussion.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The wound-care discussion is finished. The גמרא returns to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מילה of a doubtful baby or an אנדרוגינוס does not push aside שבת.

steps.title: Only a certain foreskin pushes aside שבת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the word ערלתו (his foreskin) that only a definite מילה pushes aside שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: The פסוק says "his foreskin." This teaches that only his certain foreskin pushes aside שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives the source from the פסוק for the משנה's rule. The ברייתא continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says "וביום השמיני ימול בשר ערלתו." The extra word ערלתו, "his," is read as limiting the rule: only a foreskin that is definitely subject to מילה on the eighth day pushes aside שבת. A ספק or an אנדרוגינוס is not certain, so it does not push aside שבת.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: "His foreskin" —
phrases.notes: This word is from the פסוק "וביום השמיני ימול בשר ערלתו" (ויקרא יב:ג).

phrases.english: only his certain foreskin overrides Shabbat,
phrases.notes: The ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This gives the source in the פסוק for the משנה's rule quoted in step 33.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a definite מילה on the eighth day pushes aside שבת, as learned from the word ערלתו.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for why breaking שבת for מילה is limited to clear cases, and why doubtful cases are done after שבת.
